scores.name: The Accurate Sleep Historian

scores.name: The Relocation Report
scores.gate_flags: PASS with caution: ranking-listicle format is the closest serious candidate to 'templated/mass-produced' — the shown-methodology differentiation must be executed rigorously, not just claimed, to stay clear of inauthentic-content review

top5.why: Best unit economics in the field: top-tier finance RPM ($10-25 claimed, corroborated by the meta file's $12-35 finance band), abundant sponsor fit (brokerages, budgeting apps, job boards), and the single strongest attainability proof anywhere — Edwards Economics went 0 to 358k subs in under 16 months on the exact template. 2-3 videos/week cadence means fastest time-to-YPP of any high-RPM candidate. The machine is a repeatable research-brief-to-charts pipeline. Main watch item is doom-fatigue and fast-followers, priced into sustainability.

Finance-adjacent RPM ($8-22) layered on evergreen history case studies — the rare combination of high per-view revenue AND a back catalog that appreciates. Two under-2-year channels (Fall of Nations 204k, Dr. Jonathan Tam 109k in 11 months) prove a new entrant breaks in right now. One-country-per-video is a clean repeatable system with a 100+ topic well. Verifiable-sourcing moat vs the AI-slop entrants is a durable differentiator under the 2025 policy.

The safest cash-flow machine here: near-zero cost per video (public-domain archives), 1/week solo cadence, effectively unlimited evergreen topic well, proven $4-10 history RPM with Tier-1 audience, and fresh attainability proof (Dec-2024 channel pulling 478k views on one video). Long-tail/non-Anglosphere angle means minimal head-to-head with Fascinating Horror. Lowest burnout and policy risk among the top scorers — a 3-year hold, not a trade.

The best SYSTEM in the field: DOJ/SEC press releases are a free, legally safe, self-refilling story pipeline — research risk and defamation risk are both engineered out by covering only adjudicated cases. Finance RPM plus the sharpest sponsor fit anywhere (identity protection, fraud monitoring, VPNs specifically want scam-aware audiences). Evergreen back catalog compounds. Slightly slower attainability proof than C13/C10 is the only reason it isn't higher.

Cheapest production of any high-scorer (public datasets + charts + stock b-roll, 2/week feasible), purchase-intent audience (moving, real estate, insurance) that borrows finance-adjacent CPMs, and current proof a sub-300k channel wins (Geography King, 203k views in 3 weeks, June 2026). Fast cadence = fast YPP. The caveat is real: the niche rewards slop, so the shown-methodology discipline is both the moat and the policy defense — hence the gate caution and a 5 on sustainability.

commentary: From the operator's chair, this field systematically over-weights view demand and under-weights revenue per view and catalog half-life. The gaming lane (C05-C08) is structurally handicapped no matter how good the evidence looks: median gaming RPM is $3.50 vs $12-35 in finance, so C08's 21.8M-view proof channel earns roughly what a finance channel earns on 3-4M views — its researcher is scoring audience, not business. Same trap in reverse for the AI-education pair: C03 and C26 have genuinely elite monetization (dev-tool/AI-SaaS sponsors, recurring affiliates, $15+ RPM claims) but their catalogs decay in months, which means the operator is buying a treadmill, not an asset — every week off is a revenue cut, and burnout risk at 2-3 videos/week of perpetual novelty is the highest in the field. Overrated by their researchers: C12 (the 'accuracy positioning' does not protect you from channel-level genre demotion when YouTube is actively fighting sleep-history slop — the upside is real but this is the one candidate where the platform itself is the counterparty); C20 (the long-tail thesis is unverified and the researcher admits it — entering the most saturated lane on an inference is not a business plan); C27 (the researcher's own API data shows honest entrants at 221 and 438 subs while misinfo farms take the views — that is proven negative attainability, and I scored it accordingly); C11 (huge viral ceiling but weak sponsor surface and an easily-copied format with no moat). Underrated: C16's DOJ/SEC pipeline is the closest thing here to a franchise system with engineered-out legal risk, and C09 is the lowest-variance path to a durable five-figure/month history channel. The three history/disaster/money winners share the profile I want: high or high-adjacent RPM, evergreen compounding back catalog, sub-$100 cost per video, 1+ per week solo cadence, and an originality defense grounded in primary-source research that comfortably clears the July-2025 inauthentic-content bar. Hard gates: all 28 are faceless and none is a compilation format by design; only C07 (fair-use footage weight), C12 (slop-genre adjacency), and C23 (listicle-template adjacency) carry meaningful policy-review exposure, flagged as cautions rather than failures since each has a genuine originality defense. Owner-interest lanes received no favor: history won on economics, not affinity — while gaming, the owner's other love, occupies four of the bottom ten slots.
